newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong urges Garuda to suspend its Airbus fleet.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong urges Garuda to suspend its Airbus fleet.

text.p: Hong Kong's civil aviation authority on Monday urged Garuda Indonesia Airways to suspend its Airbus Industrie A330-300 fleet because of engine problems on the aircraft.

"The Department of Civil Aviation has taken the unprecendent decision to inform the Indonesia authorities that, with immediate effect, Garuda's services to and from Hong Kong should only be operated by aircraft other than their Trent Powered A330s," it said in a statement.
"Garuda Indonesia Airways has also been informed," it added.

Hong Kong's two carriers Cathay Pacific Airways and Hong Kong Dragon Airlines grounded their 15 Airbus A330-300 fleet on Saturday, the day after a Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engine failed on a Dragonair flight, forcing the plane to make an emergency landing on one engine in the Philippines.

Hong Kong's civil aviation authority said Britain's Civil Aviation Authority (CAA), the certifying authority of the Trent 700 engine, "has also expressed the view that the Garuda A330 operations should be suspended with immediate effect".
Cathay Pacific said on Monday it expected most of its grounded Airbus A330-300 to be back up and running within three weeks.

Roland Fairfield, engineering director for Cathay Pacific, told reporters that Rolls-Royce had proposed a modification to the Trent 700 engine gearbox, which the companies hoped to start incorporating into the Airbus fleet within a week.
"We expect the aircraft to commence re-entering service on a progressive basis in approximately one week's time," he said.
